items.title: The neighbourhoods where ADHD rates are skyrocketing
items.description: ADHD diagnoses in adults have exploded across Australia since 2017. For the first time, we have the data that shows where it is — and isn't — happening.

items.title: Australia faced the same dilemma as China in 2004 but made the wrong call
items.description: While the rest of us count the cost in higher fuel costs, higher inflation and a weaker economy,  China — the actual winner of the war — will be enjoying a surge of global interest in its solar panels, wind turbines and electric vehicles.

items.title: Live: Iran rejects second round of talks with US as Trump threatens attacks
items.description: The Strait of Hormuz was declared open and then later closed again by Iran as the US continues its naval blockade of the vital waterway. Follow live.

items.title: The one man primed to benefit from a global food crisis — Vladimir Putin
items.description: With fears hunger could hit record levels, Vladimir Putin and Russia are poised to capitalise — financially and diplomatically.

items.title: The government is looking for cuts and thinks it has found its target
items.description: For the first time in this survey, more Australians are dissatisfied with the direction of the country than satisfied. The conflict between the US/Israel and Iran has delivered more than geopolitical uncertainty.

items.title: Lost, alone and out of range. How phone maps failed to save Celine Cremer
items.description: Backpacker Celine Cremer set off on a short walk with only a phone to guide her — and vanished. More than two years later, her family has an urgent message for other travellers.

items.title: Is free public transport enough to change driving habits?
items.description: Free public transport is a popular policy, but researchers say it's not enough to convince drivers to leave the car at home.

items.title: Two-thirds of Australians leave private information open to cybercriminals
items.description: New research suggests Australians are leaving themselves vulnerable to cybercrime through their public social media accounts.

items.title: US domestic violence shooting leaves eight children dead
items.description: The victims, who were shot at two homes in the US state of Louisiana, ranged in age from one to about 14 years old.

items.title: Netball star calls for pay increase after new broadcast deal
items.description: Diamonds and Melbourne Vixens star Jo Weston calls for a pay increase after a new free-to-air broadcast deal.

items.title: Could Australia make enough biofuel to keep us flying?
items.description: Australia exports billions of dollars worth of canola seed and corn husks to make sustainable jet fuel that is sold back to us. This is what it will take to make it here.

items.title: Ben Roberts-Smith issues first statement after his release on bail
items.description: War veteran Ben Roberts-Smith issues his first statement since his release on bail from a Sydney jail.

items.title: Demons cling on for epic win over Lions as Freo makes light work of Eagles
items.description: Melbourne digs deep to complete a thrilling two-point victory after a sensational tussle with Brisbane, while Fremantle claims Western Derby bragging rights with a 56-point humbling of West Coast.

items.title: Eels stun Bulldogs after having spirit and desire publicly questioned
items.description: One week after their coach publicly questioned their spirit and desire, Parramatta produces a boilover to beat the Canterbury-Bankstown Bulldogs.

items.title: 'I had no-one to talk to': 92yo Peter is trying to save his dying language
items.description: Peter is the last living speaker of the First Nations language Thiinma. When he met linguist Rosie, they used music to help keep his knowledge alive, and formed a beautiful friendship along the way.

items.title: Can you ask the council to cut down a tree?
items.description: Expert advice on how to handle council trees causing problems on private property.

items.title: Quiz: Can you tame our tricky history questions?
items.description: Is two-up actually illegal in Australia? And what movie beat Crocodile Dundee to the top of the box office in 1986?

items.title: Donald Trump might have annoyed the only ally who can help clear sea mines
items.description: The prospect of mines in the Strait of Hormuz has highlighted a gap in US naval capabilities and reinforced its need for NATO help.

items.title: Schools deemed safe after WA's biggest lithium-ion battery fire
items.description: Schools in Perth's south-east have been deemed safe for students to attend after WA's biggest lithium-ion battery fire sparked a HAZMAT warning in Maddington, which is still in place.

items.title: Man faces Melbourne court after pedestrian death at comic convention
items.description: Awer Dau, 33, faces the Melbourne Magistrates' Court on Sunday evening, charged with culpable driving causing death. He allegedly hit a 20-year-old man while driving outside the Supanova Comic Con and Gaming convention on Saturday.

items.title: How these children turned a struggle with school into ambitious art show
items.description: At an art gallery in Sydney’s inner west, a group of mostly neurodivergent children are staging their first exhibition. For many of them, it is the first time they have felt seen.

items.title: Eddie Nketia runs 100m faster than any Australian ever, but it doesn't count
items.description: Newly minted Australian sprinter Eddie Nketia breaks the national all-conditions 100m record set 23 years ago by Patrick Johnson.

items.title: Newcastle Jets crowned A-League premiers with help from arch rivals
items.description: Newcastle has claimed a maiden A-League Men's Premiers Plate after local rivals Central Coast stunned second-placed Auckland.

items.title: Fuel prices no obstacle as passionate photographers hit the road to chase auroras
items.description: For Leonie and Dean McFaull, fuel prices aren't stopping them crossing the country to add to their capture of more than 100 auroras.

items.title: Couple says loophole allowing theft from cars shipped interstate
items.description: Elihu and Amanda Del Valle say thousands of dollars worth of their belongings were stolen from the boot of their car when it was shipped from Melbourne to Perth, but police aren't able to investigate.
